rule: lower arbitrage loss at equal average fee; within 1 point, higher Pearson correlation with the keeper

sensitivity.arbCadenceNote: arbitrageur acting every 1, 2 or 15 s: venue path and per-second fees subsampled at that step; percentages against the keeper at the same step; keeperRelStep1 is the keeper's loss relative to step 1
sensitivity.weeklyNote: chosen window (300 s) against the keeper, each week simulated on its own; eta stays the five-week value, so weekly mean fees differ

feePerDollar.note: notional-weighted mean fee over the window's swaps: keeperPaid is the fee each swap paid, keeperPosted the keeper's resolved fee at the swap's second, clim the fee clim's rule would have posted at that second

sensitivity.sigmaEnvelopeNote: RiskDeskV2's envelope (x2 up, x0.8 down per report, absolute bounds) applied to each report, eta recalibrated at equal average fee

caveats: 1 s grid: the simulator cannot see sub-second races; it ranks policies, it does not predict dollars
the keeper's path is replayed as posted; clim's fee follows reports every 30 s with 2 s latency
in-sample: eta is fitted on the same five weeks the comparison runs on
no confidence interval: one price path and one run per policy
sigma comes from the same Binance (USD) path that drives the simulated arbitrageur, which can favour a sigma-driven fee; the live desk reads four venues
the on-chain sigma envelope is not modelled in the headline numbers; applied, it moves the 5-minute result from -4.38 % to -4.67 % (sensitivity.sigmaEnvelope)
framing: At equal time-average fee, clim's 5-minute rule and the keeper are comparable: -4.4 % arbitrage loss with arbitrage every second, +4.6 % every 15 s; clim charges 11.96 bp per dollar traded vs the keeper's 10.77 bp. Not a claim of better fees.
